🔦 Language models

Attention

In simple words

The part of a transformer that lets each word look at the other words and decide which of them matter for its meaning.

The key idea inside transformers. For every word (token), the model looks back at the other words of the text and works out which ones matter for understanding it, giving them more weight. That's how it keeps track of what “it” or “she” refers to, even many words later.

Example. In “The robot dropped the box because it was heavy”, attention helps the model link “it” to “the box”. Change “heavy” to “clumsy”, and “it” now points to the robot.

Related words

  • TransformerA neural network design from 2017 that uses attention to work out how the words of a text relate.
  • Next-token predictionWhat a language model does: it gives every possible next token a probability, picks one, and repeats.
  • Context windowThe amount of text, measured in tokens, that a language model can take into account at once.
